title: Zephyr Financial - Escalation Postmortem & Follow-up
next_steps: Redwood to share postmortem doc and timeline by 2026-10-01
Customer to provide KV-cache logs for 2026-09-15 window
Schedule latency benchmark with dedicated capacity (2-week window)
action_items: Sara Patel: Send consolidated postmortem slide + raw logs link (due 2026-10-01)
Liam O'Connor: Run targeted perf tests with 32k seq and share results (due 2026-10-08)
Devon Chen: Share internal rollout notes and affected service list (due 2026-10-04)
Nina Vargas: Open support ticket to track new SR and link to CRM (due 2026-09-30)
summary: Follow-up on 2026-09-15 incident where Zephyr observed intermittent 5-7s tail latencies on Redwood hosted inference for the payments fraud model. Meeting reviewed root causes (KV cache invalidation + autoscaler cold-starts for dedicated fallback), mitigations, and next steps for reliability improvements and pilot of dedicated capacity.
transcript:
[00:00] Meeting header: 2026-09-29 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Sara (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Nina (CSM), Marta (CTO - Zephyr), Rajiv (SRE), Devon (Platform), Aisha (Security)

[00:18] Sara: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanna walk through the postmortem findings from the 9/15 incident, cover what we patched and then align on pilot steps. Marta, do you wanna kick off with a quick customer perspective?

[00:34] Marta: Yeah thanks Sara. From our side the day looked like a spike in tail latencies around 11:20am which impacted merchant scoring and a few transactions timed out, customer support got alerts. It was concerning because it's intermittent, not constant, so we need confidence this wont recur.

[01:05] Rajiv: Right, uptime wasn't down but the 95th and 99th percentiles went from ~350ms to 5-7s. We saw fallback to the dedicated pool which itself had cold-starts and exacerbated latency.

[01:28] Liam: Quick correction — our initial telemetry shows two concurrent issues: an aggressive KV cache invalidation triggered by a model release and then the smart-router policy routed a subset of requests to dedicated fallback nodes which were scaled to zero and incurred container cold-starts. The combination produced those tail spikes.

[02:01] Devon: To be clear, the model release you reference was backfilled automatically as part of the roll forward, right? We did push a prompt template tweak same morning, could that have changed seq lengths?

[02:22] Liam: Could be, we saw a small uptick in average seq length for that tenant during the window (approx +12% median). That increased KV cache miss rate and longer KV population time.

[02:45] Marta: We also saw some increased burst traffic due to a marketing flow, so higher concurrency too.

[03:02] Sara: Ok so causality looks like: release + burst -> higher seq lengths and cache misses -> smart-router routed to fallback dedicated which cold-started = tail latencies. We noted the autoscaler backoff config allowed scale-to-zero which is risky for critical routes.

[03:40] Aisha: From a security/audit lens we need confirmation no data was exfiltrated and that logs were retained per our policy. We also want KMS envelope confirmation for any cached tokens.

[04:05] Liam: On logs, we collected request traces and KV cache events. No payloads left Redwood; all persisted logs are in your tenant log bucket. We'll share exact retention paths. KMS usage for ephemeral caching yes — we rotate keys per the configured schedule.

[04:35] Nina: I'll make sure the support ticket has the full log bundle link.

[05:00] Marta: One question on the dedicated fallback — can we pin warm instances or change policy to avoid scale-to-zero on critical routes?

[05:18] Liam: Yes, we have a couple of options. Short term: pin a minimum of 1-2 warm worker replicas for the dedicated fallback for your critical route. Medium term: adjust smart-router policy to consider recent cold-start penalties and prefer hosted nodes when latency SLOs are at risk. Long term: we can recommend a dedicated pool for predicted peak windows.

[06:00] Rajiv: Any quick mitigation already applied?

[06:06] Sara: We pushed a config change on 9/16 to set min_replicas=1 for the dedicated fallback and increased KV cache TTL for your tenant by 30 minutes to reduce invalidations during rolling releases. That showed improvement in staged tests.

[06:40] Devon: The longer TTL helps but it means old prefixes stay longer — is there an impact on correctness or memory usage?

[06:52] Liam: Memory uptick is minimal at current traffic; correctness OK because we version by model artifact id so staleness only arises if you require hard cache flush per release — we can instead gate invalidation on model-major-version changes.

[07:18] Marta: Good point. We'd rather not accept silent staleness; we want a deterministic invalidation policy linked to model versioning.

[07:30] Liam: Agreed — action item: Redwood will implement model-version gated KV invalidation for Zephyr's tenant as a config flag.

[07:45] Sara: Let's talk about monitoring and alerting changes to catch this earlier. Rajiv, what signals would you prefer?

[08:00] Rajiv: 95/99 latency delta > 500ms within 5m window, and an increase in KV miss rate > 15% over baseline. Also an event to show scale-to-zero resurrections.

[08:25] Nina: We can add those as dedicated alerts in Redwood console and create a dashboard for you.

[08:40] Aisha: Also ensure audit logs show who triggered config changes around model releases.

[08:52] Liam: We'll ensure change events are tied to user IDs and included in the audit trail.

[09:05] Marta: On the bench side — we want a short benchmark that reproduces the tail latencies using 32k and 8k sequences and a mix of concurrency to simulate the marketing spike.

[09:25] Liam: We'll run two scenarios: hosted baseline and dedicated-fallback with min_replicas=1, plus a dedicated pilot where we reserve capacity for 2 weeks. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and cold-start percentiles.

[09:48] Devon: How long to run the pilot? We need real traffic mirroring not synthetic ideally.

[10:00] Sara: Proposal: 2-week pilot on dedicated reserved pool with traffic mirroring and canary traffic split 10% then 50% if stable.

[10:15] Marta: That works, contingent on cost and SLA. We'll need estimated $/hour.

[10:22] Sara: We'll include cost estimates in the follow-up.

[10:30] Rajiv: Also can you confirm if the smart-router fallback policy is configurable per route? We may want different behavior for fraud scoring vs non-critical endpoints.

[10:45] Liam: Yes per-route policies are supported — we can set different routing priorities and min capacity.

[11:00] Aisha: Regarding compliance, we need SOC2 logs for the incident and a signed attestation that the event was not due to unauthorized access.

[11:12] Sara: We'll provide exported SOC2 logs for the window and a short attestation doc.

[11:25] Marta: Okay thanks. Any open concerns?

[11:30] Devon: One engineering nit — our platform saw some 502s during retries, maybe from the client side retry config. Could be client timeout too low. Would be great if Redwood can share recommended client retry/backoff settings for the SDK.

[11:48] Liam: We'll send recommended retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retries by default, per-request timeout 8s for scoring).

[12:05] Sara: Recap: Redwood to share postmortem doc + logs (by 10/01); action items assigned; pilot plan for dedicated reserved pool and cost estimates; implement model-version gated KV invalidation flag; add alerting for KV miss and tail deltas.

[12:30] Marta: Sounds good. One last ask — for the pilot, can we include an SLA uplift for the payment-scoring route?

[12:40] Nina: We'll capture SLA request and hand it to renewals team; may need contract amendment.

[12:55] Sara: Great. We'll follow up with a scheduling email and link the ticket. Thanks everyone.

[13:10] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: There are a few mis-hearings around product names (smart-router sometimes transcribed as "smart motor"). Some timestamps approximate. The raw call recording and support ticket contain exact logs and trace IDs.
